arxiv-2603-27579: Tang and He split images into cartoon and texture parts under harsh noise. Heavy-tailed noise breaks many classic decomposition tools. Their model uses a Huber loss for data fit. Total variation shapes the smooth cartoon part. A nuclear norm shapes the textured part. Low-rank priors add extra strength. Two splitting algorithms handle distinct damage types. Tests under strong noise beat rival methods. The work targets restoration of noisy images.
arxiv-2603-27879: Boushmelev and co-authors extract form factors for a Bs decay channel. The decay sends a Bs meson to a Ds star plus leptons. Four form factors describe the full process. Existing lattice data drive the demonstration. Gauge ensembles use 2+1 flavor domain-wall fermions. Three lattice spacings and several pion masses appear. Bottom quarks use a relativistic heavy quark action. Steps toward CKM and universality tests are shown.
arxiv-2603-27979: Kishawy and Chen propose RetinexDualV2, a single model for restoring ultra-high-definition images. A grounding module first extracts cues tied to each flaw, such as rain masks or dark channels. Those cues steer a Retinex split of the image into reflection and light parts, which the model then corrects. One design handles rain, noise, and low light without task-specific changes. The system placed fourth and fifth in two NTIRE 2026 challenges.
arxiv-2603-28179: Emmerich studies where points should sit on a unit interval to minimize energy under an exponential pair kernel. The kernel's shape shifts with a power q, from sharp cusps to flatter Gaussian-like forms. He asks when the best layout keeps points apart and when it collapses them to the ends. For q below 1, collisions are impossible. Past set thresholds, interior points lose their place. He gives an exact threshold for odd counts and numeric values for even ones.
arxiv-2603-28379: Ghosh derives an attraction between nucleons from the zero-point motion of a confined quantum field. For a massive scalar field between walls, he finds the interaction energy and vacuum pressure in closed form. At wide spacing, the energy does not fade away as it does for massless fields. It settles to a fixed constant set by the field's Compton wavelength. Applied at the deuteron's femtometer scale, confined pion fluctuations yield a pull between nucleons.
arxiv-2603-28579: Banfi and co-authors present EBuddy, a voice-guided workflow tool for human and machine teamwork in factories. Expert know-how is effective but hard to scale, and quality drops when steps are rebuilt ad hoc. EBuddy turns expert practice into a finite state machine. The state gives a clear frame for each spoken request and the allowed next actions. It coordinates GUI software and a collaborative robot by voice. A pilot on impeller blade inspection and repair preparation cut process time a lot.
arxiv-2603-28679: Reddig and co-authors report on a redesign of an intro AI course at a university. AI courses are hard due to abstract ideas, math, and mixed student backgrounds. Inspired by CS Unplugged, they used hands-on simulations, group coding labs, and structured reflection. Homework and exams stayed the same as the lecture version. Students in the new course reported higher attendance and stronger course impact. They also felt that tests measured their grasp better. Interviews linked the activities to engagement, confidence, and a kind class climate.
arxiv-2603-28779: Almaz and Diken introduce g-rectifying and g-normal curves in Lorentzian n-space. They build on the classic notions of rectifying curves and normal curves. Their generalization uses a g-position vector field built from an integrable function of arc length. A curve counts as g-rectifying when that vector always lies in its rectifying space. The g-normal case uses the normal space instead. They treat both spacelike and null curves. The main goal is a full characterization and classification of these curve families in Lorentzian spaces.
arxiv-2603-29079: Guseva, Skene, and Tobias develop a data driven way to discover dynamo cycle equations for low-mass stars. Realistic simulations are hard, so reduced order models are of interest. They join Dynamic Mode Decomposition, which finds magnetic structures, with Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics, which models their motion. They test the approach on a one dimensional mean-field dynamo model. The discovered equations proved more robust than weakly nonlinear analysis. They predict field saturation far from dynamo onset, even on subcritical branches where classic analysis fails.
arxiv-2603-29279: Lacey writes a comment on a recent lattice QCD claim about the critical endpoint. The target Letter used an improved equation of state with entropy contour analysis. It placed a lower bound near 450 MeV on the endpoint location. Lacey argues the method is not directly sensitive to critical behavior. Entropy contours do not probe the singular structure of the endpoint. The approach also skips the relevant scaling fields. Its assumptions fail in finite systems. The exclusion is therefore not model-independent.
arxiv-2603-29579: Hatton and co-authors present Parallelobox, a method for splitting 3D prints across several printers at once. Splitting models helps fit large prints or cut support needs. Their method uses axis-aligned bounding boxes as height fields. Boxes grow to suit a parallel printing goal, tuned by a metaheuristic search. Simple mesh clipping then cuts the model along the boxes. That yields fast decomposition with good print traits. Tests against two rival methods used simulated printing. Parallelobox won on the parallel print time metric.
arxiv-2603-29679: Hanany and co-authors describe the Higgs branches of five-dimensional Sp(k) theories with flavors. At weak or strong coupling, the branch is set by a pair of instantons. The instantons transform as pure spinors of the flavor group. Symmetry arguments constrain the Poisson structure on the branch. That makes these branches algebraic integrable systems. The symplectic form degenerates when the spinor annihilators overlap. At infinite coupling, the branch layers align with instanton weights. That alignment yields a nonzero magnetization and gives the instantons mass.
arxiv-2603-29879: Weisenbach and the CROCS Collaboration present a playful first data release on the Hubble tension. Planck and SH0ES values for the Hubble constant clash at 5.5 sigma. Their tongue-in-cheek analysis blames imperial biasing systematics in both surveys. Converting to metric units, they claim, reconciles the two camps. Their merged value lands at 69.00 plus or minus 0.420 in metric units. They declare the Hubble tension ended for good.
arxiv-2604-00179: Bai, Doan, and Romberg study a projected, linear, two-time-scale stochastic approximation run with fixed step sizes and Polyak-Ruppert averaging. They prove a mean-square error bound split into an approximation error from the constrained subspace and a statistical error fading at a sublinear rate. The bound's constants keep the subspace choice separate from the averaging horizon, resting on stability margins for restricted settings and a condition that the coupling can be inverted. Experiments on synthetic and reinforcement-learning problems show the theory.
arxiv-2604-00279: Liu and eight colleagues split the modality gap into centroid and distribution gaps. The distribution gap predicts task quality far better than the misleading raw gap, with R-squared values of 0.986 against 0.691. Their TPC-CMA framework, a three-phase curriculum for cross-modal alignment, shrinks centroid offsets and reshapes distributional structure with staged scheduling. With a low alignment target, the gap falls about 67 percent for about a 5 percent cost. Stronger alignment cuts the gap about 82 percent, improving clustering and captioning by about 57 percent.
arxiv-2604-00479: Tian and colleagues study why reinforcement learning helps vision-language reasoning, and where it narrows it. Reinforcement-trained models reason deeper but along narrower paths, while base models think less sharply on any one path yet range more broadly. The team traces this gap through training dynamics, finding that group relative policy optimisation tends toward diversity collapse: models settle early on a small set of reasoning strategies and discard most alternatives. Their paper proposes incentivising divergent thinking to counter that narrowing.
arxiv-2604-00979: Wang and team propose the Dignified Peer framework for language models, fighting the Evasive Servant failure mode: models sweet-talk flawed user beliefs, dodging blame behind stock notes. Dignified Peer counters fawning with honesty and trust, and dodging with empathy and ideas. Its PersonaKnob data set ranks many persona tastes. A lenient bounded Lagrangian DPO method levels persona sides to prevent conduct collapse, and a test-based tuned Item Response Theory scale splits latent persona skill from judge biases.
arxiv-2604-01079: Skandylas and Asplund present a way to auto-generate cybersecurity drills mocking company IT systems. Training humans and software agents to protect key systems needs drills varying in size, scope, objectives, and difficulty. Each drill's scope, context, setting, and plot are key to running it. Their way makes many drills varied across size, scope, difficulty, twists, and mix. They also release as open source a mock and virtual setup running drills from them, plus a dataset of 100000 sample drills.
arxiv-2604-01279: Bright-Thonney and colleagues introduce Sven, a method for neural networks that exploits how loss splits across data points. Rather than collapsing loss to one scalar before updating parameters, Sven treats residuals from each data point as goals to satisfy at once. It finds the smallest update via the loss Jacobian's Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. That pseudoinverse is approximated by a truncated singular value decomposition keeping only the k top ways. Tests on regression, classification, and small transformer modeling show Sven rivals Adam, Muon, and K-FAC.
arxiv-2604-01679: Nguyen and colleagues propose BTS-rPPG, a time method using Orthogonal Butterfly Temporal Shifting. Time moves remain hard, as many methods rely on time shifting or convolutional ops aggregating information mostly from nearby frames. Inspired by the FFT pattern, BTS sets up structured frame links via an XOR butterfly pairing schedule. They present orthogonal feature transfer, filtering source parts against target context before shifting, keeping only the orthogonal part for cross-frame sending. Tests on many benchmark datasets show BTS-rPPG lifts long-range temporal models.
arxiv-2604-01779: Hubarava and Gao build a framework for controllable text simplification, steering open models to target readability and compression with fine-tuning and control tokens. Control is often handled as a decoding problem and judged by metrics that miss control, while data and evaluation constrain it. Across three model families and four domains, smaller models prove competitive, but reliable control depends on training data varying enough in the target attribute. Readability control is learned, while compression control lags for lack of signal variation, and metrics prove insufficient, motivating error-based measures.
arxiv-2604-01879: Mishra and Kumar show in theory how linked light-and-sound cavities can send signals one way only. One-way flow matters for isolators, routing and fine sensing, and their design drives paired optomechanical cavities, which swap light signals for sound vibrations, with phase-set lasers. Unlike one-way sound transport, which needs both loss and broken time-reversal symmetry, the light-sound swap breaks neither yet still runs one way, thanks to path-dependent imbalance. Tuning the laser phase gap pushed isolation to 40 dB in their calculations.
arxiv-2604-02079: Wang, Huang, Deng, Sun, Zhou and Zhao tackle testing for apps that users reshape themselves. Their ALADDIN framework walks through phone screens, triggers the features each user asked for, and checks results with oracles guided by a language model. Tested on six popular apps with sound and faulty requests, it caught errors in features built to order. The work points from manager set products toward apps shaped by the people who use them.
arxiv-2604-02179: Walbert and colleagues study how sampling layout shapes uncertainty in earth science random field models. They fold discrete sampling patterns into a spectral maximum likelihood estimator with analytic error math. Examples span ragged regions, structured instrument sweeps and scattered gaps. Studies favor spreading samples over a growing domain rather than densifying infill for cutting estimator bias and variance. They also show the Matern class behaves well and test fit against Gaussian, stationary and isotropic ideals.
arxiv-2604-02479: Martin and team test whether an Earth model can make lifelike post wildfire imagery from burn masks without special training. They compare six setups varying build, prompt plan and color matching. Inpainting beats full tile making on all metrics, with a set prompt giving the best spatial match at Burn IoU near 0.46. Color matching gives the lowest color distance at some cost to burn contrast, and VLM aided work rivals hand crafted prompts.
arxiv-2604-02579: Franco and two colleagues analyze scaling limits for two particle systems on a segment fed by a finite reservoir at the left end. The systems are independent random walks and symmetric exclusion processes. A tuning parameter theta drives a phase transition in the left boundary condition. Below one, the condition is Neumann with a deposit that empties in the limit. Above one, it becomes Dirichlet with a reservoir that grows without bound and acts as a heat bath. The right end stays Neumann throughout.
arxiv-2604-02679: Fan and three colleagues solve the prescribed Hermitian-Yang-Mills tensor problem for Higgs bundles over compact complex manifolds. Start from a smooth Hermitian metric whose tensor is positive definite. Then any Hermitian positive definite target tensor is attained by a unique smooth Hermitian metric. The result pins down the metric exactly, with no freedom left. The paper also proves Chern number inequalities with explicit bounds for Higgs bundles.
arxiv-2604-02779: Zhang and five colleagues build a fully vision-based system for drones to fly through narrow, irregular gaps. Old methods need explicit gap measurement, while recent end-to-end methods assume regular gap shapes and generalize poorly. Their system maps depth images straight to controls in SE(3), using differentiable simulation, a stop-gradient operator, and a bimodal initialization distribution. Two helper predictors for gap-crossing success and safe passage add safety. Tests span simulation and real-world flights, showing strong generalization.
arxiv-2604-03079: Bao and Chitnis introduce EEspice, an open-source circuit simulator whose modular design splits device model testing into replaceable kernels. Standard parallel work spreads transistors across cores, but stamping, adding device inputs to the shared system matrix, bottlenecks when cores compete for the same matrix spots. EEspice partitions MOSFET units into independent color groups processed in parallel, enabling a parallel stamping plan that clears the bottleneck. On a 64-core workstation, it runs up to 45 times faster than single-thread performance when conflicts are low.
arxiv-2604-03279: Ranjith and colleagues co-optimize a production speech-synthesis model with Tenstorrent hardware so low-precision compute keeps audio clean. Their Lightning V2 system holds over 95 percent fidelity under low-fidelity compute and deploys more than 80 percent BlockFloat8 without measurable quality loss. Against an NVIDIA L40S baseline, it cuts on-prem accelerator cost about fourfold at equal throughput.
arxiv-2604-03379: Chou and Hamaker study Coxeter theory for mu-involutions, the combinatorial objects indexing Borel orbits in the variety of complete quadrics. They describe atoms, prove an exchange lemma, and give transposition-like operators characterizing Bruhat order. Orbit closures sit inside the flag variety, and the corresponding Schubert polynomials expand as a multiplicity-free sum when one involution refines another.
arxiv-2604-03779: Renzo Soatto and colleagues built CountsDiff, a diffusion model for count data that live on the natural numbers. It extends the Blackout framework with a direct survival-probability schedule and explicit loss weights, plus continuous-time training, classifier-free guidance, and remasking steps that allow non-monotone reverse paths. Tests on image sets and single-cell RNA imputation matched or beat a leading discrete generative model and top imputation methods.
arxiv-2604-03979: Takashi Kamihigashi and John Stachurski gave a single necessary and sufficient condition for steady-state spreads in monotone Markov models that stay stable in all cases. Earlier work offered a jumble of old rules made for set uses, on spaces that may run without bounds. Their test pairs long-run shrinking with a tight path, spanning closed and open spaces, step time and smooth time, and curved maps tied to group state. Uses span wage moves, belief-based learning with belief shocks, and income flows with Pareto tails.
arxiv-2604-04079: Mohamed Afouene Melki and team built a multi-AUV plan for lasting sea Internet of Things work. The task joins path control with sound comms, framed as a Markov choice process spanning motion, drive-aware energy use, sound-based energy transfer, and Age of Information rules. A single PPO policy steers multiple craft under docking and safety limits. Tests against rule-of-thumb rivals showed lower average Age of Information with fairer, better data hauls.
arxiv-2604-04479: Liu and colleagues ask how large language models can support policy researchers. Building on a workflow for LLM-assisted thematic analysis of online forums, the team studies 11 policy researchers using an early prototype, seen as a quick, rough-and-ready research input. They then extend and scale the workflow to millions of Reddit posts and 1,058 chatbot-led interview transcripts, treating these as rich, scalable data for policy discourse. Comparing synthesized themes with authoritative policy reports reveals alignments and divergences, with implications for researchers adopting LLM-assisted workflows.
arxiv-2604-04579: Trinh and three colleagues present Firebolt-VL, a vision-language model pairing images with text cheaply. Most multimodal models lean on Transformer cross-attention, whose quadratic cost slows use on phones and cameras. It swaps its Transformer decoder for a Liquid Foundation Model one. A Token-Grid Correlation links text tokens to image patches and steers the state-space model with FiLM conditioning. The design spotlights image regions matching the text prompt while keeping inference linear in time. Tests across benchmarks show fine-grained understanding with better efficiency.
arxiv-2604-04679: Lu, Rollett and Dayal study how twin boundary motion starts in a 2D lattice with box-shaped unit cells, for rational and irrational twins. Using slow shear loading and stability analysis, they show motion onset is signaled by a nonlocal linear instability. The instability is marked by the loss of the lowest Hessian eigenvalue, whose eigenmode predicts the shifts that start motion. Irrational twins need lower critical shear stress to start moving than rational ones. They show unusual ways, such as microtwin growth at right angles to the twin edge.
arxiv-2604-04879: Ermann, Chepelianskii, and Shepelyansky revisit the 1876 Boltzmann-Loschmidt dispute. It asked how irreversible statistics could arise from reversible atomic motion. They show, by analysis and simulation, that quantum chaos diffusion of cold atoms or ions can be run backward in time. In a trapped, pulsed optical lattice, the reversal reaches up to 100 percent efficiency. Classical motion fails that test, since tiny errors explode, and the authors argue present experiments could stage this quantum reversal.
arxiv-2604-04979: Kovács studies pruning for coding agents, which read long tool outputs though only a small part matters next. Given a focused query and one tool output, the task is to return the smallest verbatim evidence block worth inspecting next. He builds a benchmark of 11,477 examples from SWE-bench interactions and synthetic tool outputs, with a curated 618-example test set. Fine-tuning Qwen 3.5 2B with LoRA, his model reaches 0.86 recall while removing 92 percent of input tokens, beating a larger zero-shot model by 11 recall points.
arxiv-2604-05079: Yang and five co-authors propose SVAgent, a storyline-guided cross-modal multi-agent framework for long video understanding. Video question answering requires integrating spatial, time, and semantic cues to capture video dynamics. Most methods locate key frames to answer questions rather than thinking through the changing storyline as humans do. Humans interpret videos through clear storylines, an ability crucial for robust, grounded predictions. SVAgent's storyline agent builds a story from frames suggested by a refining agent, letting the system reason through story flow rather than single frames.
arxiv-2604-05479: Kerrison and seventeen colleagues report a 21-centimeter hydrogen absorption line at redshift 0.882 in front of quasar PKS 0405-385, found by the FLASH survey. Long-slit spectra confirm matching magnesium and iron lines plus two further metal systems at higher redshifts, though the gas hosts stay unpinned. Fresh radio monitoring revises the quasar's size upward past 0.3 parsecs with no repeat of its once-famous rapid flickering.
arxiv-2604-05679: Alonso-Orán, Granero-Belinchón, and Yanes Pérez derive a one-dimensional model for blood flow in viscoelastic arteries. They prove local well-posedness for strong solutions under general parameters and periodic data. In the purely elastic BBM regime, small data yield global existence with exponential decay, and numerics explore viscoelastic and amplitude regimes.
arxiv-2604-05779: Lee and five colleagues teach language models when to say they do not know, using instance-level knowledge scores from multi-sampled inference. Learning signals scale with existing knowledge while out-of-scope queries draw explicit uncertainty replies. The model keeps accuracy on answerable questions and discriminates known from unknown instances more reliably.
arxiv-2604-05879: Mazziotta comments on a recent solar gamma-ray study, comparing it with a 2020 FLUKA Monte Carlo run on cosmic-ray hits to the solar atmosphere. The earlier work modeled hadron hits, magnetic-field effects, cascades, and Fermi-LAT checks across particles. He maps agreements, flags modeling gaps, and shows how the two approaches jointly light up high-energy solar disk emission.
arxiv-2604-05979: Willebeek-LeMair and Woolsey tackle a control flaw in multirotor craft. A free-fall command can leave the craft's desired orientation undefined. Their 2026 paper reworks a robust baseline controller for flat motion. The new design fits a pivoted thruster that pushes in one direction only. It steers the thruster output toward a small zone around the target value. Simulations show the adapted design recovers the baseline controller's guarantees in practice.
arxiv-2604-06079: Lin and colleagues' 2026 paper tackles graphics program synthesis, turning static visuals back into editable TikZ code. Image-TikZ sets often fail on executability and visual alignment, and fidelity benchmarks are missing. Their closed-loop framework offers SciTikZ-230K, a dataset from an execution-centred engine across 11 fields. It also offers SciTikZ-Bench, a benchmark from basic shapes to complex hierarchical diagrams. Dual self-consistency learning uses round-trip verification to penalize bad code and boost self-consistency. Their trained model, SciTikZer-8B, beats Gemini-2.5-Pro and massive rivals.
arxiv-2604-06279: Zhang and eight colleagues introduce Plasma GraphRAG, pairing graph retrieval with LLMs for physics-grounded parameter picks in gyrokinetic runs. Manual paper reviews make picks slow and uneven. It builds a knowledge graph from plasma literature and retrieves over graph entities and relations, yielding context-aware ranges. Across comprehensiveness, diversity, grounding, hallucination, and empowerment metrics, it beats vanilla RAG by over 10 percent and cuts hallucination rates by up to 25 percent. The authors offer it as a method for discovery across data-rich domains.
arxiv-2604-06579: Crisci, Schuler, Jordan, and Scholz describe SonicDB S6, a production Rust database built on Verkle tries for the Sonic blockchain, which issues a block every 300 milliseconds. Exploiting the chain's non-forking property, occupancy-aware node designs cut live storage by about 98 percent. Delta nodes recording only changed slots cut archive storage by 95 percent. Batched updates and parallel commitment work deliver more than three times the throughput of a persistent Geth Verkle baseline while holding production block pace.
arxiv-2604-06779: Shekhar and three colleagues fight lineage collapse in reward-guided diffusion samplers. Monte Carlo runs let a few high-reward particles dominate quickly, killing diversity and sample quality. Their variance-decomposition framework splits continuation from residual variance, tracing collapse to offspring-count variance under multinomial resampling. VASR pairs variance-optimal mass allocation with systematic resampling, and VASR-Max biases selection harder for noisy rewards. Both run training-free, in parallel, with low overhead, beating SMC methods by up to 26 percent on FID and running 66 times faster than MCTS methods.
arxiv-2604-06879: Liquori, Mendler, and Stolze extend CCS with priority-guarded actions and clocks to reach determinacy. Milner's CCS is a non-deterministic process algebra whose chapter 11 sought a subset where every agent is confluent. Fixed rules for Esterel and SL do not map cleanly onto Milner's confluence theory, since CCS cannot express causality and shared-memory multi-threading with reaction to absence in a compositional way. The authors enrich confluence with coherence, a new concept that lets their extension encode synchronous languages like Esterel piece by piece.
arxiv-2604-07079: Kasem and five colleagues present MARVEL, a three step pipeline for finding text with both words and images when the query needs hard reasoning. The best sight plus word search tool scores poorly on the MM-BRIGHT test set, well below strong word only tools. MARVEL first widens the query with a language model, then searches with a retriever tuned for hard queries, then re ranks hits with step by step thought. On twenty nine technical fields it beats the best sight plus word tool by a clear margin.
arxiv-2604-07279: Liu and five colleagues present Mem3R, a streaming 3D reconstruction model built for long video sequences in robotics and augmented reality. It splits the job in two: a fast-weight memory tracks the camera, while an explicit token state maps geometry, curbing drift and forgetting over time. The design also trims the model from 793 million to 644 million parameters against CUT3R. Paired with an improved update scheme, it cuts trajectory error by up to 39 percent on sequences of 500 to 1000 frames.
arxiv-2604-07379: Li and three colleagues move resonator design from periodic to aperiodic order with quasicrystals. Periodic crystals already give soft clamping via stopbands, but aperiodic designs had no clear route to find such bands. Their data-driven search predicts high-quality resonators in quasicrystal layouts. A 12-fold design hits a quality factor near ten million with sub-nanogram mass at megahertz rates. Its force sensitivity beats prior two-dimensional phononic crystals.
arxiv-2604-07979: Wang and three colleagues argue that differentiable hybrid force fields resolve a trilemma in autonomous electrolyte discovery. A discovery engine must screen fast, predict properties well, and refine itself online from new data. Classical empirical force fields run fast but lean on error cancellation, while standard machine-learning potentials cost too much compute. Hybrid fields fuse physics-based functional shapes with neural-network short-range fixes. Grounded in energy decomposition analysis, models like PhyNEO-Electrolyte and ByteFF-Pol generalize zero-shot to bulk phases, reaching tens of nanoseconds per day.
arxiv-2604-08079: van der Sluis and Azzopardi test whether searching helps consumers act on their desire to shop responsibly. Good intentions often fail to become responsible behavior, and information seeking, or its absence, contributes to that intention-behavior gap. The team hypothesizes that searching can bridge the gap toward purchases better aligned with values. In a task-based study, 308 participants searched for details on one of eight ethical aspects of a product they were shopping for. Active searching raised the importance shoppers assigned to ethical aspects, driven by spotting ethical considerations.
arxiv-2604-08279: Kikawa presents SPIROS, a sleek, precise, easy, and rapid optical tool for particle physics detectors. Unlike broad systems like GEANT4, SPIROS offers a light engine and a friendly interface tuned for optical processes: flashes, Cherenkov emission, and photon flow with bounce, bending, spread, uptake, and catching. Detector geometries import straight from 3D CAD models, and every setting, matter, faces, sources, and sensors alike, is set in one human-readable input file. Checks against GEANT4 agree well on photon making.
arxiv-2604-08379: Bosschaart and Olofsson test whether light scattering patterns from debris discs truly reveal dust grain traits. Using synthetic images built from known dust behavior, they recover the patterns and compare them with the known inputs across grain sizes, tilts, and disc thicknesses. Even with perfect geometry knowledge, recovered patterns stray far from the true ones, because narrow angle coverage hides strong forward peaks. Scattering patterns from real images, they conclude, are effective observed quantities, not direct dust measures.
arxiv-2604-08479: Gueorguieva and six colleagues find that language model empathy follows a well liked template, while human empathy varies more freely. From a taxonomy of ten empathic tactics, including validating feelings and paraphrasing, they compare 3,265 machine replies with 1,290 human ones across two studies. A fixed tactic sequence matches 83 to 90 percent of machine replies and covers most of each matched reply, raising questions about the future of machine generated empathy.
arxiv-2604-08579: Sarkar tests whether vision and language encoders trained alone share spectral structure, using maps between graph Laplacian bases. The two models' spectra look alike, with a scaled distance of just 0.043, hinting at similar inner structure. Yet their vector bases barely align, with near zero diagonal dominance and large mismatch, a gap he calls the spectral complexity orientation gap.
arxiv-2604-08979: Liu and four colleagues improve access for blind and low-vision readers by replacing pitch-only sonification with spatial audio that places sounds around the listener. Pitch turns data into tones and conveys trends and comparisons, but it hides fine detail such as whether a value is negative and what it is. In a study with 26 participants, ten of them blind or low-vision, it beat pitch on fine tasks like recognizing signs and exact values. It matched pitch on trend reading and trailed only on value comparison.
arxiv-2604-09179: Morselli, Tebaldi, and Zanasi build a step-by-step model of clutch action in a two-speed powershift gearbox for real-time control and simulation. The core works out the exact torque needed to engage a clutch, covering both a single clutch and two clutches locking at once. Around that core they develop control logic for the engage and release phases. Simulation tests show the step-by-step version suits real-time use better than the earlier continuous-time version.
arxiv-2604-09279: Chen, Hu, and Yang generalize quasi-projective dimension from modules over associative rings to complexes of modules. Basic properties follow, including a comparison with projective dimension and an Auslander-Buchsbaum formula for complexes of finite dimension. Several conditions are given for a commutative local ring to be a complete intersection, when every module has finite dimension. This answers part of an open question posed by Gheibi, Jorgensen, and Takahashi. The quotient by a regular sequence is also studied, with partial results toward the change-of-rings question.
arxiv-2604-09379: Zischler, Mecozzi, and Antonelli provide closed-form rules for Raman boosting and inter-channel driven Raman effects in space-division split links. In optical networks, the Raman effect enables spread boosting but also causes warping through inter-channel effects. In single-mode fibers these effects are known, but matching closed-form rules for freely coupled such links have been lacking. The authors provide closed-form rules for common designs with freely coupled matched mode groups, adding mode coupling and curve effects, with great match with tests.
arxiv-2604-09479: Killip, Marsden, and Vişan give continuum Calogero-Moser models a Hamiltonian footing. They place the models on the Hardy space that recent well-posedness work names as their natural phase space. A new symplectic form turns the focusing and defocusing models, on the line and the torus, into Hamiltonian systems. Their known conserved quantities are shown to commute with each other. The structure yields a fresh well-posedness argument for the critical space. It also reveals links to Carleman's inequality and the planar isoperimetric problem.
arxiv-2604-09779: Neufeld, Perry, and Witten review selective inference, for questions that are a function of the data. Guesses and values are often picked from the data rather than set in advance, and standard methods then fail to deliver nominal range cover. Three cases need picked fixes: a winner, a tree-region mean, and a gap in means between a pair of clusters. The authors argue that limited cover matters for science here, then review methods providing them, showing them in tests and on single-cell RNA data.
arxiv-2604-09879: Nampoothiry and three co-authors present Topo-ADV, the first shape-driven attack on 3D point-cloud networks, testing the idea that kept shape means kept meaning. The method treats hole structure as a new weak spot, tuning shape diagrams through smooth shape forms. It jointly tunes shape gap, wrong labels, and shape stealth, keeping hit clouds plausible to the eye. Tests on ModelNet40, ShapeNet Part, and ScanObjectNN with PointNet and DGCNN reach up to 100 percent attack success, beating state-of-the-art methods on stealth.
arxiv-2604-09979: Yao, Li, and Liu introduce a minimal embedding model for representation collapse, where embeddings lose structure and distinct inputs blur together. The model's dynamics and fixed points admit closed-form analysis of collapse via label-embedding contraction. The model holds steady for perfectly classifiable data, but frustrated samples trigger collapse through a slow scale following early gains. A shared projection head and stop-gradient enable non-collapsed solutions and class separation under frustration. The same dynamics appear in a linear teacher-student model, showing the theory holds beyond embedding settings.
arxiv-2604-10479: Hair and Sahai build public key encryption on nearly fully corrupted puzzle systems. Their scheme leans on two constraint puzzles where nearly every output is random noise. One is a new large alphabet predicate puzzle on strongly spreading graphs. The other is the classic kXOR puzzle, again under near total corruption. A planted trapdoor plus a fresh error code with efficient decoding seals the scheme.
arxiv-2604-10579: Zhang and five colleagues grow robot demo variety from 3D shape matches. Imitation learners stall when training shapes vary too little. Their AffordGen frame links matching keypoints across huge 3D mesh sets to spawn new paths. The affordance aware set then trains a closed loop vision motor policy. Tests in sim and real rooms show high wins and zero shot jumps to unseen objects.
arxiv-2604-10679: Jeon, Wong, and Chae study a fluid reconfigurable surface assisting a Rydberg atomic receiver that reads strength, not phase. Unlike coherent systems, they show, the best setting depends on the receiver's nonlinear readout. Symbol reading is limited by leftover quadrature leakage after reference matching, so they shape the channel from the receiver side rather than tuning the channel alone. Their design jointly tunes surface ports, phase shifts, and the transmit beamformer by alternating search. Tests show fast settling, steady error-rate gains, and near-best results at lower cost.
arxiv-2604-10779: Zhang studies West's stack-sorting map on permutations whose last entry is also their least. For each such permutation he introduces a stack-sorting tableau, a new combinatorial object that becomes the key ingredient in the first polynomial-time algorithm for counting t-stack-sortable permutations in this class. He then establishes a precise relationship between the map's behavior on this restricted set and on all permutations.
arxiv-2604-11179: Deppisch builds a blind multichannel speech enhancer that keeps direction intact. A compact neural network, OnlineSpatialNet, gauges the noise pattern across a microphone array. A direction-preserving Wiener filter then cleans the speech while holding on to spatial cues for beamforming and sound localization. Tests beat a mask-based baseline and come close to oracle results with far fewer parameters and less computation.
arxiv-2604-11579: Kim and four colleagues tackle tactile localization: finding image regions matching a touch input's material. Existing touch-vision methods use global alignment and miss fine local matches, while datasets skew to close-up, low-diversity images. Their model learns local touch-vision alignment through dense cross-modal feature links, producing tactile saliency maps for touch-based material segmentation. They add wild multi-material scene images and a material-diversity pairing plan, plus two new tactile-grounded segmentation datasets. Experiments show substantial gains over prior touch-vision methods.
arxiv-2604-11679: Munk and 83 colleagues report the FOMO25 challenge on brain MRI foundation models. Clinical data are messy and noisy, labels costly, and prior models leaned on small pretraining sets and clean benchmarks. FOMO25 supplied FOMO60K and tested models on clinical data in few-shot and out-of-domain settings for infarcts, meningiomas, and brain age. Nineteen models from sixteen teams ran a standardized pipeline. Self-supervised pretraining improved generalization under domain shift, with the strongest out-of-domain models beating supervised baselines, though no single objective helped every task.
arxiv-2604-11779: Parc and eight colleagues review research on super-Earths and sub-Neptunes, the most common known exoplanets, from 2014 to 2025. They use Kepler and TESS light curves plus ground-based velocity surveys with HARPS, ESPRESSO, and NIRPS, and theory on interiors, makeup, formation, and growth. Early JWST studies of atmospheres, they argue, are sharpening the picture while still testing current formation theories.
arxiv-2604-11879: McKay, Barger, Cowie, and Bauer follow up dusty star-forming galaxies in the GOODS-S field with ALMA spectroscopy of an 870-micron-selected sample. Linescans confirm or identify redshifts for 26 sources, bringing secure or tentative redshifts to 54 of 75 galaxies, or 72 percent. Above 2.5 millijanskys the sample is 97 percent complete, the highest completeness yet for an unbiased sample at that flux limit. Photometric redshift methods all show outlier rates above 20 percent and tend to overshoot, inflating high-redshift counts. At most about 6 percent lie beyond redshift 4, and at most 1 percent beyond redshift 5.
arxiv-2604-12079: Chung and three colleagues address hardware-induced nonlinearities in compute-in-memory chips, where device spread strains results. Their hardware-aware framework uses hyperdimensional computing, framing encoding to minimise the Frobenius norm between an ideal kernel and its hardware twin, with joint calibration of hypervectors. Applied to QuantHD, it reaches 84 percent accuracy under severe perturbations, a 48 percent increase over naive QuantHD. It also preserves RelHD results on Cora, a 5.4-fold improvement over naive RelHD under nonlinear settings, keeping the approach robust and symbolic on emerging hardware.
arxiv-2604-12279: Kozenko and three colleagues numerically optimize a symmetric controlled-Z gate using the Rydberg blockade in neutral atoms, aiming for robustness against Rabi frequency variation. Analytically defined laser pulse phase profiles make the scheme nearly ten times more robust than earlier protocols. A smooth pulse shape optimized for finite blockade strength suits single-photon and two-photon setups, and the design handles individually addressed atoms, easing residual thermal motion effects.
arxiv-2604-12479: Shanyong Wang and four colleagues align language models with individual preferences that conflict and change. General preference tuning misses how one person's values shift over time. Their Preference-Paired Fine-Tuning method trains on paired preferences instead of single ones. A new Value Conflict Dilemma dataset supplies scenarios with clashing preferences. The method beats single-preference training, reaching up to 96.6 percent on multi-choice tasks. With little user history, it still improves user-specific alignment by 44.76 percent over single-preference models.
arxiv-2604-13179: Tran, Nguyen, and Nghiem present HUANet, a neural network that speeds up constrained convex optimization by unrolling the ADMM algorithm into learned layers. Each layer carries a hard-constrained network whose correction step meets the affine equalities of the primal subproblem. Optimality rules join a self-taught training loss, and tests on benchmark problems and a control task confirm faster solving.
arxiv-2604-13479: Rathukohe Mudiyanselage and Cheung propose Dynamic Focal Attention, which learns class hardness inside cross-attention for uneven tissue segmentation. Count-based weights assume rare classes are hard, yet hardness comes from shape variety, boundary blur, and context likeness. It adds a learnable per-class bias to attention logits, reweighting signs before output rather than gradients after it. Starting from a count-based start, it lifts Dice and IoU on three benchmarks, matching or beating a two-stage rival with no extra step.
arxiv-2604-13679: Arlow and eight colleagues track hydrogen gas in luminous compact blue galaxies with the CHILES survey. The survey spent 856 hours observing the COSMOS field, reaching redshift 0.48. By stacking faint signals, the team estimates average hydrogen masses at three redshifts, and it also detects two galaxies directly. Average gas mass shows no strong evolution across that range. Gas fractions stay constant, yet depletion times run nearly ten times shorter than in normal star-forming galaxies.
arxiv-2604-13779: Silbernagel and Weiss propose an integer-valued moving-average random field, INMA, for count data spread across space. Count data means whole numbers, like counts of events per area. They derive closed-form formulas for its marginal distribution and spatial dependence, for any model order and the multilateral case. Formulas cover bivariate distributions and autocovariances. The field can carry a Poisson marginal, and different dependence structures are possible. A real-world example illustrates the model, and an INMA approximation to a given dependence pattern is proposed.
arxiv-2604-13879: Wang and Ma hunt for the source of KM3-230213A, the most energetic neutrino ever recorded, at 220 PeV. They test every plausible gamma-ray burst against the neutrino's position, allowing for the angular uncertainty on both sides, and find a larger set of matching bursts than earlier work. For each match they compute a Lorentz-invariance-violation scale, folding in redshift and energy uncertainties.
arxiv-2604-13979: Abdallah and colleagues present GLOW, a hybrid system for open-world question answering over incomplete knowledge graphs. A graph neural network proposes top candidate answers from graph structure, and a language model reasons over those candidates plus serialized facts in a structured prompt, with no retrieval or fine-tuning. On a new 1,000-question benchmark and standard sets, improvements reach up to 53.3 percent, averaging 38 percent.
arxiv-2604-14279: Dersy and Schwartz move beyond the dilute instanton gas for the double well by using exact saddles at finite Euclidean time. At every instanton order, the whole resurgent pattern lies in a Picard-Lefschetz contour integral over quasi-zero modes with a geometric meaning. Finite temperature proves essential: the dilute gas reaches only ground-state splitting, while the exact computation yields non-perturbative splittings for every excited state with level-number dependence. Weierstrass elliptic functions, Lamé operators, and Picard-Fuchs equations form a framework overlapping and complementing Exact WKB.
arxiv-2604-14379: Zhang, Wang, and Zou tackle diffusion-model alignment when human taste spans several goals, such as beauty and text-image match. Multi-goal methods either pay for costly joint tuning or fuse separately tuned models at sampling time, needing reward values and adding approximation error. Their retraining-free MSDDA framework derives the best reverse denoising distribution in closed form from single-goal base models, step by step. The team proves this sampling-time goal equals step-level reinforcement tuning exactly, and tests show it beats existing sampling-time methods.
arxiv-2604-14979: Keller, Lenz, and Schmidt review recent work on graphs viewed at large scale and their Laplace operators. They focus on Liouville theorems, which ask when only flat, steady functions can survive across an endless graph. They also cover recurrence, the question of whether walks keep returning, and how edge terms describe Dirichlet forms. The survey pulls these threads together to show how far-off graph shape steers local behavior.
arxiv-2604-15079: Tsai gives a short proof of Harish-Chandra's celebrated result on local integrability of complex characters for p-adic reductive groups. Built on local character expansions, the proof recasts integrability in algebraic form that also works for some other coefficients. It covers cases the literature seems to miss and shows each character is locally integrable to a stated power above one. The argument thus widens and simplifies a classic theorem.
arxiv-2604-15179: Carrasco-Arango, Badia, and Garcia-Saez build and simulate a quantum Metropolis-Hastings algorithm for realistic circuits. Quantum walks promise faster mixing for Markov Chain Monte Carlo, but practical circuit versions remain hard. Their implementation follows the Claudon framework with changes needed for a workable circuit model, covering the full workflow to prepare a stationary distribution. The team shows those changes are essential to recover correct stationary behavior, while flagging both promise and present limits.
arxiv-2604-15279: García-Raigada, Jorba, and Iserte present DQR, a runtime that schedules fragments of split quantum circuits as ordinary jobs on hybrid supercomputing systems. A backend-neutral descriptor exposes each fragment's structure, and a wave-based coordinator pipelines them without blocking. Tests on a 32-qubit circuit show faster completion than a single-processor baseline, plus automatic rerouting when hardware rejects a fragment.
arxiv-2604-15379: Chowdhary and nine colleagues present Fleet, a task model for chiplet-based GPUs whose flat programming models waste cache locality. Fleet binds work and data to chiplets through Chiplet-tasks that coordinate via shared L2 cache, with persistent per-chiplet scheduling. On AMD's MI350 running Qwen3-8B, decode latency falls 1.3 to 1.5 times versus vLLM at small batches, and HBM traffic drops up to 37 percent at larger ones.
arxiv-2604-15579: Hong and four colleagues argue that domain-specific AI agents need symbolic guardrails, not just training-based or neural ones that lower but cannot rule out unsafe tool calls. Reviewing 80 agent safety benchmarks, they find 85 percent state no verifiable requirements. On three benchmarks, 74 percent of requirements prove symbolically enforceable, mostly by simple low-cost checks, and symbolic guardrails raise safety without costing utility.
arxiv-2604-15979: Wang and four colleagues present MMGait, a multi-modal gait benchmark that identifies people at a distance from how they walk, without needing cooperation. It joins data from five sensors, RGB, depth, infrared, LiDAR, and 4D radar, into twelve modalities and 334,060 sequences from 725 subjects. Tests span single-modal, cross-modal, and multi-modal settings to probe robustness and complementarity. The authors add a unified task, Omni Multi-Modal Gait Recognition, plus a baseline, OmniGait, that learns a shared embedding space across modalities.
arxiv-2604-16079: Briq and four colleagues investigate what drives quality and diversity in flow-matching models: architecture or training datasets. On CelebA-HQ, flow matching stays stable even after pruning 50 percent of the dataset, preserving quality and diversity. Pruning barely shifts the latent representation: full-data and pruned-data models map the same seed to visually similar outputs. Similar stability holds when changing architecture or training setup, with the latent representation maintained throughout. The results quantify this stability and help explain why flow-matching models prove reliable under perturbations.
arxiv-2604-16179: Van Hülst and five colleagues apply matrix product state methods, a compression tool for turbulent fields, to two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection, where heat drives flow. Earlier work compressed isothermal turbulence well, but buoyancy-driven flow with active heat coupling was untested. Their dynamical runs in the compressed format, and a prior split of simulation snapshots, show how the size needed to represent the flow grows without levelling off.
arxiv-2604-16279: Chennakesavalu and seven co-authors test large language models for small-molecule drug design, where benchmarks matching real-world use have been missing. They build a suite of lab-grounded tasks with trait forecasting, form changes, and drug design, framed as reinforcement learning setups for unified testing and post-training. Across three model groups, frontier models grow more skilled at lab tasks, yet much room remains, above all with low data. Reward-based post-training lifts a smaller model to frontier-level standing.
arxiv-2604-16779: Roy and Alam open Q-SINDy, a quantum-kernel framework for sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics. They spot coefficient eating, where quantum features absorb mass owed to the poly basis and corrupt formula rebuild. Removing the polynomial column-space part of quantum features kills this bias exactly, checked to machine limit. Across six systems and three quantum designs, cleaned Q-SINDy matches vanilla shape rebuild while raw boost cuts hit rates by up to 100 percent. A motion-aware diagnostic predicts cannibalization size, and cleaning stays robust under hardware noise.
arxiv-2604-16879: Yang and seven colleagues tackle synthetic-image detection, where tools trained on known fakes often fail on unfamiliar generators. Their I2P framework picks out the vision-model layer carrying the strongest forgery clues. It then limits task tuning to a low-sensitivity part of the model so pretrained knowledge stays intact, giving steadier results on fresh sources.
arxiv-2604-17079: Star, Aquilina, and Lin audit how language models offer social support across multi-turn conversations, where users reveal their situation gradually. Support-seeking stories from five Reddit communities are split into fragments and revealed turn by turn, with each reply coded under the Social Support Behavior Code. Across more than 6,200 turns with two mid-scale models, support mix shifts with estimated distress: teaching falls as distress rises, a pattern holding across both architectures.
arxiv-2604-17679: Hu, Siu, and Chen combine offline Hamilton-Jacobi reachability with online graph search for safe, fast indoor planar robot movement. Graph search is widely used for its breadth and proofs under valid heuristics, but its cost grows rapidly with search-space size, blocking real-time planning in dynamic settings. Prebuilt value functions serve as useful guides and proactive safety constraints, spreading online graph-search work. Graph search in turn lets safety logic enter online planning, overcoming its long-standing need for full setting knowledge. Broad sim tests support the method.
arxiv-2604-18179: Liu offers a commit-open protocol to catch hosted-model providers that quietly swap in a cheaper model. Probe-after-return checks fail because a dishonest provider can route the probe to the advertised model. Under the new scheme, the provider first commits to a sparse-autoencoder sketch of its served output, then a verifier opens random positions and scores them against a public probe library. All 17 tested attackers are rejected at one shared threshold, while a white-box attack and a forgery attack also fail to close the gap.
arxiv-2604-18479: Paul, Banerjee, Bhowmik, and Kundu present a warm-start quantum-classical framework for MIMO data detection with high-order modulation. Classical maximum-likelihood detection grows exponentially hard, and Gray coding turns the problem into higher-order binary optimization. A warm start from a low-rank semidefinite relaxation, solved by block coordinate descent, seeds a linear-ramp quantum approximate optimization routine. Simulations beat classical methods on symbol error rate, converge faster than standard QAOA, and run near-optimally on IBM hardware at low signal-to-noise ratios.
arxiv-2604-18779: Tong, Di, and Zhang present Mango, a web navigation method with multiple agents, using a website's structure to choose starting points. Existing agents usually start from the root URL and can fall into traps, wander into irrelevant branches, or miss targets within budget. Mango treats URL choice as a bandit problem, uses Thompson Sampling to allocate budget, and stores past attempts in episodic memory. On WebVoyager it reaches about 64 percent success with GPT-5-mini, and on WebWalkerQA it beats the best baseline by about 27 percentage points.
arxiv-2604-19179: Mantovan and 20 colleagues observe super-Neptune TOI-1710 b in transit, measuring its Rossiter-McLaughlin effect with HARPS-N and GIANO-B. Tidally detached at about 36 stellar radii, it preserves its obliquity. They estimate a true obliquity of about 149 degrees, indicating retrograde motion around a cool star, the only such known system. The misalignment favors eccentric migration for this super-Neptune, challenging claims of a minor role here. Without a stellar companion, the misalignment likely arose through scattering, Kozai-Lidov oscillations, and tidal circularisation.
arxiv-2604-19279: Schwerter and colleagues test whether borrowing strength from a previous student cohort improves early warnings in a later cohort. They fit weekly Bayesian models to six engagement indicators from a blended first-year mathematics course, using either flat default priors or informative priors taken from the earlier cohort of 307 students. In the target cohort of 323, the prior-informed logistic models cut misclassification by 22 percent and false negatives by 38 percent in week 3.
arxiv-2604-19479: Duarte and colleagues study distance minimization to a real algebraic variety under a polyhedral norm. Each point of the variety has a Voronoi cell whose shape depends on the normal space at the point and the inner normal fan of the polyhedral ball. For codimension-one varieties, they split the variety into sets of points whose Voronoi cones share the same dimension. They prove this split is a stratification with semialgebraic strata, and they close with an algebraic description of the medial axis.
arxiv-2604-19879: Dyndal and Harland-Lang study ion breakup in glancing LHC collisions, where ions pass at a distance and exchange light rather than hitting head-on. Such breakup can spray hadrons into the detector and spoil the clean, empty signature of exclusive particle events. They work out the effect for muon pairs and for J/psi mesons made in this clean mode. Once counted, the effect clears up long-standing gaps between theory and data.
arxiv-2604-20079: Gupta, Deshpande, and Chakraborty test post-training quantization on diffusion language models for coding, a sparsely explored robustness question. They apply GPTQ and a modified Hessian-aware method, HAWQ, to the CoDA coding model and compare against Qwen3-1.7B, its autoregressive counterpart. CoDA proves more robust at low bitwidths of two to four bits, with smaller accuracy drops on HumanEval and MBPP. Mixed-precision HAWQ settings trade accuracy, latency, and memory smoothly, suggesting diffusion models may suit efficient deployment.
arxiv-2604-20679: Daniele Corradetti and Renato Corradetti present a full extension of the Hopfield memory model for CA3, a brain region. It uses ten groups, forty-seven parts, multi-rule plasticity, and a cholinergic cycle. Tested at N equals 256, the full design shows three signs absent from a minimal Hopfield control. It shows multi-attractor behavior at K equals 5, selective recall of paired items, and reduced variance under clean upstream input. Those signs show up in every regime tested and never in the minimal control, showing they come from the design.
arxiv-2604-20779: Baumann, Padmakumar, Li, Yang, Yang, and Koyejo introduce SWE-chat, a large collection of real coding agent sessions gathered from open-source developers. The dataset currently contains almost 18,000 sessions, more than 229,000 user prompts, and 2 million agent tool calls. They find that coding patterns are bimodal: in 41 percent of sessions, agents author all committed code, while in 25 percent, humans write all code themselves. Only 59 percent of agent-produced code reaches user commits, while code written by agents carries more security flaws than human-authored code.
arxiv-2604-21679: Hahn and six colleagues spent six months inside a multinational security operations centre, studying why staff distrust new tools. Working beside practitioners, they built language-model companion tools fitted to daily routines, cutting disruption and making outputs easier to interpret. Early scepticism gave way to steady use, and the team explains the shift through co-creation, drawing on Nonaka's SECI model, rather than through the technology alone.
arxiv-2604-22079: Liu reports for the Belle and Belle II collaborations on b to s decays. The experiments have accumulated a dataset of 1.2 inverse attobarns of electron-positron to B anti-B collisions at the Upsilon(4S) resonance. This includes the reinterpretation of B+ to K+ nu anti-nu and the first inclusive measurement of B to Xs nu anti-nu with missing energy directly from B decays. It also includes searches with missing energy from tau decays, such as B0 to K*0 tau+ tau- and B0 to KS0 tau+ tau-.
arxiv-2604-22279: Mahmudov studies operator equations in a Hilbert space, seeking near-solutions with one exact part. The aim is to match one set component exactly while approximating the rest. He proves solvability for every positive tolerance exactly when a smoothed term tends to zero. Dropping any structural assumption breaks that equivalence. A Galerkin scheme restores approximate solvability even when a related map fails to invert. In plain terms, the work pins down the exact test for a near-solution that hits one target spot-on.
arxiv-2604-22579: Mouton and six colleagues ask whether medical-image networks learn useful nonrobust features, telling patterns humans cannot read and hostile tweaks can break. Models trained only on those features score above chance across five MedMNIST sorting tasks, confirming their value in training data. Hardened models leaning on robust features give up some in-distribution accuracy but perform much better under data shifts on MedMNIST-C. The upshot is a trade-off: those features lift accuracy yet harm out-of-distribution performance, so the balance should follow the use setting.
arxiv-2604-22679: Sharma and Molamohammadi study supply-chain bias checks in AI hiring. AI hiring raises bias and accountability worries, prompting the EU AI Act, NYC Local Law 144, and Colorado's AI Act. Past work looks at bias through technical or regulatory lenses, yet misses a challenge: AI hiring systems run in supply chains splitting duty across vendors, developers, platforms, and deployers. Split duties create two problems. First, bias springs from component links, not parts, yet setups block joint checks. A resume parser fair alone can still feed discrimination when combined.
arxiv-2604-22779: Gao and colleagues teach language models to say no when a question lies past their edge, without falling into too much caution. Their KARL plan gauges the edge on the fly from group scores, backing right answers or guided holding back as the edge shifts. A two-stage training plan first maps the edge, then turns past-edge errors into saying no while keeping accuracy high.
arxiv-2604-22979: Cotti and twelve co-authors build a pipeline for Wi-Fi-based human activity recognition that can be read causally. A categorical variational autoencoder packs signal windows into a compact discrete code, frozen as a map to latent trajectories. Causal discovery on those paths yields temporal dependency graphs, turned into Linear Temporal Logic rules for a fully symbolic, deterministic classifier with no learned head. Results show competitive performance while keeping time and causal structure, as a viable alternative to end-to-end black-box models.
arxiv-2604-23379: Ates, Chapman, Estes, and Jackson study random walks on sea dragon trees, a family of trees whose branching points all lie on one central path. For several classes of these trees they compute the average number of steps a walk takes to reach a chosen absorbing vertex, using Markov chain methods. They also prove further results about such averages on graphs in general.
arxiv-2604-23579: Xie and colleagues present CineAGI, a staged framework for auto movie making that keeps characters true across scenes. One module drafts film plans with character profiles, a character-first pipeline tracks identities across shots, and a sync layer lines up dialogue, looks, and music frame by frame. Overall consistency rises 40 percent over baselines in the team's tests.
arxiv-2604-23979: Yang and five colleagues present SDSL-Solver, a distributed solver for the sparse linear systems that dominate interior point optimization. It pairs Krylov methods with filtering and diagonal fixes to build strong preconditioners, offers Block Jacobi and bordered block diagonal parallel schemes for different matrix types, and reuses preconditioners across steps. On large benchmarks it runs several times faster than PETSc on matching nodes.
arxiv-2604-24079: Yang and four colleagues find language model personas in discourse structure rather than surface word choice. Most discovery methods read dialogue as flat token strings and lean on lexical or style cues. Their framework models bridging inference, the implicit links that tie utterances through shared knowledge and coherence, as knowledge graphs. Across reasoning backbones and models up to 80 billion parameters, these graphs give stronger coherence and steadier persona identification than frequency or style baselines.
arxiv-2604-24179: Bueno, Hirlimann, and Kasneci tackle hate speech in memes with prompted weak supervision. Single end-to-end prompts must resolve target, stance, implicitness, and irony at once, and multilingual cues make the task harder. Their method splits understanding into targeted questions with constrained answers, using a quantized Qwen3 vision-language model to label homophobia and transphobia. It beats direct classification, ranking first in English, second in Chinese, and third in Hindi, and error-driven refinement further cuts redundancy.
arxiv-2604-24279: Luo and Zhou introduce slow-branch susceptibility for functional dismantling of relaxation. Robustness is not set by connectivity, since the slow mode can change spectral type under damage. From projected motion, the key observable is the real part of the selected Laplacian branch, setting long-time decay. Node deletion is dimension compression, yielding a modal susceptibility score for first-order decay reduction from slow mode support. In the reciprocal limit it reduces to the weighted Fiedler sector, and tests show it finds gaps centrality attacks miss.
arxiv-2604-24479: Ataei and three colleagues present Zero-to-CAD, a framework making CAD build series without real data. Making becomes an agentic search: a language model in a feedback-driven CAD setup writes, runs, and checks code. Tools and docs lookup promote soundness and range. The approach yields about one million executable, readable, editable CAD series beyond sketch-and-extrude workflows. A subset of 100,000 models is chosen for geometric range. Fine-tuning a vision-language model on synthetic data rebuilds editable CAD programs from images, beating strong baselines including GPT-5.2.
arxiv-2604-24579: Tran-Truong and Le argue that single benchmark scores hide how language-model agents actually succeed or fail over time. Their TraceToChain pipeline fits execution traces to an absorbing Markov chain, a model of step-by-step states ending in success or failure. It adds fit checks, credible intervals and bootstrap intervals to quantify uncertainty. Tests on seven controlled agent frameworks with a strict fit-test split show held-out reliability curves closely matching the model's predictions.
arxiv-2604-24779: Friedman builds a superposition framework for relativistic gravity in Extended Relativity, a Lorentz-covariant theory in flat spacetime. Gravity fields appear as shifts from the Minkowski metric for single sources. Multi-source fields are built by a superposition rule linear in source parameters. The resulting metric keeps Lorentz covariance and passes classical general-relativity tests in the right limits. He derives the field superposed from multiple moving sources and studies its near- and far-zone traits.
arxiv-2604-24979: Estay, Noto and Ulloa ask how heat-linked material properties affect cold water convection. Water shows an anomalous density equation near freezing, with rising viscosity and falling conductivity. They simulate cold water convection between freezing and the density peak. Two cases split the effects: constant versus heat-dependent viscosity and conductivity. The main result is a shift in fluid temperature, with the equation of state and material properties pushing apart. The former dominates, giving a drop up to 0.08 degrees Celsius at high Rayleigh number. Convection onset is barely affected.
arxiv-2604-25079: Adiya and four colleagues classify Lie symmetries of time-fractional telegraph systems with varying coefficients. Such systems model transport with memory in heat flow, viscoelastic waves and charge flow. The symmetry type turns on how the transport coefficient relates to the potential function, giving three distinct classes. For each class they build optimal subalgebra systems, reduce the equations to fractional ordinary forms and state exact solutions in closed form.
arxiv-2604-25379: Lim, Jeong and Lee put forth Safe-Support Q-Learning, barring unsafe visits. Most safe RL ways roam into unsafe states. Their frame uses a safe-set-backed behavior policy, so paths stay safe while roaming enough to learn, with no need for near-optimal behavior. They train Q-function and policy apart. A KL-tuned Bellman target keeps Q-values near behavior policy. A parametric extraction step nears the best policy. Tests show steady learning, well-tuned values, and safer behavior at par or better than baselines.
arxiv-2604-25579: Arguin, Bailey and Roberts prove conditional upper bounds for large deviations and moments of the Riemann zeta function, assuming the Riemann Hypothesis. They bound the share of times where the zeta value on the critical line exceeds a power of log T. The constant in the bound grows doubly exponentially in the exponent. That bound caps the even moments of zeta by a matching power of log T, recovering the bound of Harper. The proof builds on a recursive scheme with Bourgade and Radziwill.
arxiv-2604-25779: Kitkana and Arora test whether subliminal learning lasts across many training steps, using MNIST auxiliary logit distillation. A student can pick up an unintended teacher trait while distilling only on no-class logits. Single-step theory credits alignment between trait and distillation gradients. But it does not guarantee alignment lasts. The authors show alignment stays weakly but consistently positive through training and causally drives trait acquisition. A mitigation called liminal training weakens alignment yet fails to stop acquisition here.
arxiv-2604-25979: Parisel analyzes the Currier A/B split in the Voynich Manuscript. First, a Beta-Binomial mixture model on character-pair ratios across 185 folios works blind to Currier's labels. It selects two components and scores 89 percent accuracy on held-out folio labels. That confirms the distinction is genuine. Second, the A/B contrast reflects a higher-dimensional system at low resolution. Its main component is a boolean switch fixed per folio, setting the vowel after ch and sh. Template identity explains 92 percent of variance.
arxiv-2604-26179: Byramji and three colleagues gave a unified way to build explicit distributions that restricted computers cannot sample. Their robust extractors stay sound even when a few points break the entropy condition, forcing every output of low-depth circuits, small-space sources, and similar models far from the target. The method also yields the first such distribution against low-degree polynomial sources over the binary field.
arxiv-2604-26779: Iso and seventeen colleagues speed reinforcement-learning post-training rollouts with system-integrated speculative decoding, a lossless method keeping the target model's output distribution. Rollout making increasingly slows frontier model training, and many efficiency methods change the rollout or optimization setup instead. Built in NeMo-RL with a vLLM backend for sync and async runs, speculative decoding lifts rollout throughput nearly twofold at 8-billion scale under sync training. Models project up to two and a half times end-to-end training speedup at 235-billion scale when combined with async training.
arxiv-2604-26879: Fazzini reports three recent LHCb results testing whether leptons couple universally to electroweak bosons, as the Standard Model predicts. Charged-current decays of bottom hadrons offer large rates and hadronic uncertainties. The contribution presents the first measurement of the branching-fraction ratio R(D**). It also gives the branching fraction for a lambda baryon decaying to a proton, muon, and antineutrino, plus form-factor parameters from a B-meson decay to a charm meson, muon, and neutrino. Together they test the Standard Model and possible new physics.
arxiv-2604-26979: Moureaux and two colleagues present a tool for N-ary in-memory crossbar architectures that retrieve matrix-vector results with minimal assumptions. Such computing performs matrix-vector products in memory arrays, promising energy gains. XOR and MNIST tasks run on an array of 4 by 4 magnetic tunnel junctions, with MNIST accuracy near 94 percent versus a higher software baseline. PCA reduction sharply cuts operations and lifts the baseline, for only a modest crossbar score cost. Weight quantization is the top error source, and cell noise proves less harmful than errors.
arxiv-2604-27179: Faust and Scheunemann propose EMSL, a simple and efficient reduced strain-space model order method. It targets hyperelastic sample blocks. The method groups the material domain into regions of similar behavior. It queries the material routine at one reference strain per region. Unlike the earlier E3C approach, it samples those strains only once per load increment. It uses typical values guessed from data. The stiffness at a reference point and strain measures then drive rapid online runs.
arxiv-2604-27679: Inoue and five colleagues demonstrate a parametrically driven iSWAP gate at zero flux bias between detuned transmon qubits coupled through a capacitively shunted double-transmon coupler. Using a simple flux-drive pulse without predistortion, they reach an average gate fidelity of 99.92 percent in 112 ns of total gate time. The high fidelity matches weak qubit-coupler hybridization plus weak effective ZZ coupling during the gate. Simulations reproduce the seen coupling rate and effective ZZ coupling, backing the theoretical model for both spectral and time-domain dynamics.
arxiv-2604-27779: F. Tolea and M. Tolea model solid-state phase change as nucleation and growth of plain plates. Squares, cubes, or lamellae grow alike until a random cap or a clash with earlier plates stops them. The reverse change drops smaller plates first while larger plates stay, so a later change yields a modified mix, a memory effect. Extending a flat model to cubes and lamellae, they introduce the size mass ratio as memory measure. Memory proves robust in all shapes but stronger in two dimensions than in three.
arxiv-2604-27979: Seoev and colleagues ask where arbitrage chances on blockchains actually come from, rather than how traders exploit them. They build four attribution methods and test them on over a million Polygon blocks, finding most atomic arbitrage traces to a single source transaction. Creation proves highly concentrated in a few protocols, a pattern useful to designers curbing leakage, validators ordering transactions and analysts gauging ecosystem health.
arxiv-2604-28179: Dunn Beltran's team removes the need for breath-hold protocols in bronchoscopic navigation, where breathing shifts the airway by millimetres and breaks CT alignment. Matching paired inhale-exhale CT scans reduces breathing motion to a single phase per frame, and a light reader reads that phase from scope video alone. Built into a mesh-based Gaussian splatting system, the method rebuilds the airway all through the breathing cycle. It pins targets down within clinical tolerances, far faster to train than unconstrained baselines.
arxiv-2605-00279:
Zawad Yalmie Sazid, Robert Abbas, and Sasa Maric compare machine learning models for spotting intrusions in intelligent transport systems. Connected vehicles, roadside units, and 5G links widen the surface attackers can reach, while roadside edge nodes have limited computing power. Protection therefore has to run close to the traffic itself.

The paper proposes a trust-aware federated hybrid detection framework. At each edge site, a random forest, a decision tree, and a linear support vector machine each learn their own view of the traffic. A central server then merges the local updates, weighting each site by trust. The design aims at proactive, low-latency defense that can work without constant human control.
arxiv-2605-00479:
Tom Kimpson, Mark B. Flegg, and Jennifer A. Flegg ask whether cheaper math can speed the stochastic simulation algorithm, the exact workhorse for random processes in biology. It crawls event by event, and large runs make it costly. Weather and climate work had already gained from working at fewer bits, which prompted the test.

Across five classic models from biology, their first approach, scoring reaction rates in 16-bit while keeping totals at 32-bit, matched the 64-bit standard closely. Doing it all in 16-bit brought in steady biases under plain rounding, sometimes badly. Rounding that uses chance, plus a scaling step, removed those biases and brought the match back across the board. The payoff is smaller memory footprints and a modest wall-clock speedup on current hardware, with larger gains likely on chips built for 16-bit math.
arxiv-2605-00579:
Kamila Szewczyk speeds up a small, crucial step inside data compression. Fast range coders and asymmetric numeral systems replace slow division with bit shifts, which works only when symbol frequencies are normalized to sum to a power of two. Normalization always distorts the distribution slightly, costing compression ratio, measured as added Kullback-Leibler divergence. Szewczyk shows the methods in current use are suboptimal twice over, in both running time and distortion.

The proposed method runs in time linear in the number of symbols and achieves the smallest divergence any normalization can reach. It rests on solving a separable concave optimization problem, which Szewczyk notes may interest readers beyond compression. The result is a drop-in improvement to a primitive that sits underneath widely used entropy coders: same interface, provably best fidelity to the original frequencies, and a faster algorithm to compute it.
arxiv-2605-00779:
Elsa Barrio-Torres and five co-authors test how well climate models reproduce summer air circulation over the Iberian Peninsula. They examine thirty-six historical CMIP6 model runs for 1979 to 2005 against ERA5 reanalysis, using the Lamb Weather Type scheme to classify daily circulation. Their framework also checks how types persist and change from one day to the next.

Daily frequencies alone kept sixteen runs, but adding persistence and transition checks narrowed the set to twelve. Models from the EC-Earth3 family performed best and most consistently, led by one aerchem run. Skill was stronger in the northwest and weaker in central and southern Mediterranean areas. The authors argue transition checks select models far better than daily counts alone.
arxiv-2605-00979:
Andreas Stergiou and Nicolas P. D. Sawaya prove that hardware-efficient quantum gates are universal for making states inside tight subspaces, such as those with fixed particle number or spin. Simulating physical systems on near-term quantum computers often requires staying inside such subspaces. Using Lie algebra methods, they pin down Pauli Z dressing as the key mechanism: commutators of overlapping gates produce projectors that split rotations into generators spanning the full algebra.

Adding separate complex phases extends the result from real to arbitrary complex state preparation. An efficient Jacobian criterion verifies whether a circuit can explore any direction from almost any parameter setting. Applications include Hubbard models and molecular structure, plus a completeness proof for a particle-number ansatz and symmetry-preserving circuits for a fuzzy sphere model.
arxiv-2605-01679:
Joydeb Kumar Sana detects falls among older people from wearable sensor data without leaking the private activity records behind the training.
